ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p353/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p353/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p353/r2.claim: The discourse moves from day and night as models of developmental trials, to reassurance, promised better times, examples of past divine help, and duties arising from those favours.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p353/r2.anchor: Following is the sequence of the discourse

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p354/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p354/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p354/r1.claim: The future success promised to the Prophet is followed by reminders of earlier deliverance and spiritual blessing, then guidance to fulfil the duties those favours impose.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p354/r1.anchor: At the end, he is guided to fulfil the obligations

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p358/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p358/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p358/r1.claim: Al-ākhirah and al-ūlā here mean later and earlier phases of the mission, or its future and present, rather than the Hereafter and this world.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p358/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p358/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p358/r2.claim: The verse explains the preceding assurance: current hardship will change, and the mission’s future will surpass its past and present.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p358/r2.anchor: the current circumstances will soon change

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p358/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p358/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p358/r3.claim: The comprehensive good promised includes Islam’s supremacy, the conquest of Mecca, enemy humiliation, and mass conversion; preceding and following sūrahs also allude to these outcomes.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p358/r3.anchor: It gathers in it the aspects of supremacy and victory of Islam, the conquest of Makkah, humiliation of the enemies and people entering the folds of Islam in multitudes

QUSHAYRI:v3p429/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p429/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p429/r8.claim: The Hereafter is better because its gifts exceed this world's; these include intercession, the Basin, and the robe of unity.
QUSHAYRI:v3p429/r8.anchor: ما يعطيك في الآخرة خير لك مما يعطيك في الدنيا

BINTSHATI:v1p37/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p37/r1.speaker: الرازي
BINTSHATI:v1p37/r1.claim: Al-Razi says the pause cannot mean removal of prophethood; at most it signaled death, which would be good for the Prophet because of his afterlife reward.
BINTSHATI:v1p37/r1.anchor: أن إنقطاع الوحي لا يجوز أن يكون لعزل عن النبوة، بل أقصى ما في هذا الباب أنه أمارة الموت

BINTSHATI:v1p37/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p37/r2.speaker: الرازي
BINTSHATI:v1p37/r2.claim: Al-Razi says that the Prophet's receipt of the verse's honor was followed by assurance of still greater honor in the afterlife.
BINTSHATI:v1p37/r2.anchor: كالرازي الذي ذكر فيها وجوهاً ثلاثة

BINTSHATI:v1p37/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p37/r3.speaker: الرازي
BINTSHATI:v1p37/r3.claim: Al-Razi labels as his own speculation that the Prophet's future conditions would be better than his past ones, then lists reasons involving divine pleasure, his community, witness, and lasting afterlife gifts.
BINTSHATI:v1p37/r3.anchor: وقد صدره الرازي بقوله: وهو ما يخطر ببالي - وللأحوال الآتية خير لك من الماضية

BINTSHATI:v1p37/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p37/r4.speaker: الشيخ محمد عبده
BINTSHATI:v1p37/r4.claim: Abduh reads al-akhira and al-ula as the end and beginning of the Prophet's mission: renewed revelation would complete the religion and God's blessing.
BINTSHATI:v1p37/r4.anchor: ولنهاية أمرك خير لك من بدايته

BINTSHATI:v1p38/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p38/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p38/r1.claim: Although al-akhira usually means the afterlife in the Qur'an, contextual evidence can give it another sense, as in al-milla al-akhira.
BINTSHATI:v1p38/r1.anchor: يغلب أنها للدار أو الحياة الآخرة، مقابلة للدنيا

BINTSHATI:v1p38/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p38/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p38/r2.claim: The paired Qur'anic expressions al-akhira wa-l-ula usually name the two lives; this surah applies them particularly to Muhammad's fear of abandonment and assures him that his future is better.
BINTSHATI:v1p38/r2.anchor: فنرى آية الضحى تنفرد عنها بأنها خاصة بمحمد - صلى الله عليه وسلم -، في حالة بعينها

BINTSHATI:v1p38/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p38/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p38/r3.claim: Verse 5 completes the reassurance: God did not leave the Prophet in the past, and his future is better.
BINTSHATI:v1p38/r3.anchor: يتكامل بها التجلي الإلهي على المصطفى: ما تركك فيما مضى، وللآخرة خير لك من الأولى

BIQAI-FULL:v8p453/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p453/r6.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
BIQAI-FULL:v8p453/r6.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr says the predestination discussion could cause fear, so God reassured His dearest servant by recounting his favor and the good of both lives.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p453/r6.anchor: أنس تعالى أحب عباده إليه وأعظمهم منزلة لديه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p455/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p455/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p455/r2.claim: The many human paths reduce to belief or disbelief and to Paradise or Hell, as paired creation and flight toward God indicate.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p455/r2.anchor: ولانحصار السبل وإن تشعبت في طريقي

NAHHAS:v5p249/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p249/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p249/r9.claim: Akhayr was shortened to khayr because the form was frequent.
NAHHAS:v5p249/r9.anchor: الأصل أخير ثم خفف لكثرة الاستعمال

DURR-FULL:v8p541/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p541/r7.speaker: ابن عباس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p541/r7.claim: The Prophet was shown the conquests that would open to his community after him and was pleased; the verse says the afterlife is better than the first life.
DURR-FULL:v8p541/r7.anchor: وأخرج الطبراني في الأوسط والبيهقي في الدلائل عن ابن عباس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p493#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p493#2/r11.speaker: ابن إسحاق وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p493#2/r11.claim: Ibn Ishaq and others take the Hereafter as better than this world.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p493#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p493#2/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p493#2/r12.claim: Alternatively, the verse compares the Prophet's condition before and after the surah, promising worldly victory and prominence.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p493#2/r12.anchor: ويحتمل أن يريد حاليه في الدنيا قبل نزول السورة وبعدها

TABATABAI:93:3-7/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:93:3-7/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:93:3-7/r4.claim: The afterlife being better is an ascent from the preceding reassurance: the Prophet remains in divine favor throughout earthly life, and his next life is better than this one.
TABATABAI:93:3-7/r4.anchor: في معنى الترقي بالنسبة إلى ما تفيده الآية السابقة من كونه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم على ما هو عليه

THALABI:v10p223/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p223/r11.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p223/r11.claim: The afterlife is better for Muhammad than the first life.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p411/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p411/r4.speaker: بعض المفسرين
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p411/r4.claim: Some interpreters take al-ākhirah as the Hereafter, the life beyond this world.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p411/r4.anchor: إنها ما هو غير الدنيا بمعنى الدار الآخرة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p411/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p411/r5.speaker: بعض المفسرين
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p411/r5.claim: Others understand al-ākhirah broadly as whatever comes later in life, not necessarily the Resurrection.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p411/r5.anchor: وقسم قال انها كل ما يستقبل من الحياة على العموم

ELMALILI:93:2-4#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:93:2-4#2/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:93:2-4#2/r5.claim: He reads al-ākhira broadly as every later stage in the Prophet's life being better than its earlier stage, culminating in the afterlife, rather than only the hereafter opposed to worldly life.
ELMALILI:93:2-4#2/r5.anchor: Ve her hâlde âhire bulunduğun her hâlin sonu

ELMALILI:93:2-4#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:93:2-4#2/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:93:2-4#2/r6.claim: The verse does not mean that dying immediately would be better for Muhammad; that would wrongly imply his later worldly life brought no greater good.
ELMALILI:93:2-4#2/r6.anchor: “şu anda ölmek senin için daha hayırlıdır” demek olur

ELMALILI:93:2-4#2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:93:2-4#2/r7.speaker: ابن عطية، müfessirîn
ELMALILI:93:2-4#2/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya and other commentators take the verse as saying the end of Muhammad's affair is better than its beginning, with strength and rank continually rising.
ELMALILI:93:2-4#2/r7.anchor: İbn Atıyye ve daha bir kısım müfessirîn bunu bidâyet ve nihâyet mânasıyla

ELMALILI:93:2-4#2/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:93:2-4#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس، رسول الله
ELMALILI:93:2-4#2/r8.claim: Al-Ṭabarānī and al-Bayhaqī transmit from Ibn ʿAbbās that the Prophet was shown future conquests for his community, rejoiced, and then this verse was revealed.
ELMALILI:93:2-4#2/r8.anchor: Taberânî’nin Evsat’ta, Beyhakī’nin Delâil’de İbn Abbas’tan tahric eyledikleri şu hadîse

ELMALILI:93:2-4#2/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:93:2-4#2/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:93:2-4#2/r9.claim: The future realization of the promise was shown as a vision, a miracle; the later conquests of the Persian and Byzantine realms and Constantinople are examples.
ELMALILI:93:2-4#2/r9.anchor: Kisrâ ve Kayser mülklerinin ve Kostantiniyye’nin fethi hakkındaki haberler

ELMALILI:93:2-4#2/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:93:2-4#2/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:93:2-4#2/r10.claim: Other commentators take al-ākhira in its familiar sense of the afterlife and al-ūlā as this world; he says this can fit the context if worldly life is also understood as blessed until death.
ELMALILI:93:2-4#2/r10.anchor: Şu hâlde diğer bir kısım müfessirînin dedikleri gibi burada da “âhiret” mâruf olduğu üzere “dünya” mukabili

ELMALILI:93:2-4#2/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:93:2-4#2/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:93:2-4#2/r11.claim: The comparative hayr entails that worldly life is itself good, while the broader reading additionally conveys steady growth in good from one stage to the next.
ELMALILI:93:2-4#2/r11.anchor: Bu mazmun “hayr” kelimesinin ism-i tafdil olmasından müstebân olur

ELMALILI:93:2-4#2/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:93:2-4#2/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:93:2-4#2/r12.claim: The restriction for you contrasts Muhammad with hostile unbelievers; his believing followers share his hereafter's good, while even unbelievers benefit from his worldly good.
ELMALILI:93:2-4#2/r12.anchor: lâm-ı ihtisâsın mânası da cemî‘-i mâ‘adâya nazaran değil, ezâ eden kâfirlere nazaran kasrdır

QASHANI:93:4-8/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:93:4-8/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:93:4-8/r1.claim: The later state is disclosure after concealment and intensified longing, better than the earlier state because it is secure from selfhood’s residual variegation.
QASHANI:93:4-8/r1.anchor: وللحالة الآخرة التي هي التجلي بعد الاحتجاب واشتداد الشوق

SULAMI:v2p400#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p400#3/r1.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v2p400#3/r1.claim: The Prophet's stored afterlife station and intercession are better than the prophethood and messengerhood given him in this world.
SULAMI:v2p400#3/r1.anchor: قال سهل : ما ادخرت في الآخرة من المقام المحمود ومحل الشفاعة خير

SULAMI:v2p400#3/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p400#3/r2.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p400#3/r2.claim: The Prophet's reserved honors exceed what creatures witness: he is an obeyed intercessor and the one authorized to speak when others cannot.
SULAMI:v2p400#3/r2.anchor: وقال بعضهم : ما لك عندي من مخزون الكرامات اجل مما يشاهده الخلق

SULAMI:v2p400#3/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p400#3/r3.speaker: يحيى بن معاذ
SULAMI:v2p400#3/r3.claim: Both worlds require hardship, so one should seek the more lasting of them.
SULAMI:v2p400#3/r3.anchor: وقال يحيى بن معاذ : الآخرة لا تنال إلا بالمشقة والدنيا لا تنال إلا بالمشقة

SULAMI:v2p400#3/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p400#3/r4.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v2p400#3/r4.claim: Leaving the world is difficult, but losing the afterlife is more difficult.
SULAMI:v2p400#3/r4.anchor: وقال الجنيد رحمه الله : ترك الدنيا شديد ، وفوت الآخرة اشد

TUSTARI:93:4/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:93:4/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:93:4/r1.claim: God has stored for the Prophet a greater station of praise and intercession in the afterlife than the prophethood and message granted in this world.
TUSTARI:93:4/r1.anchor: قال: ادخرت لك من المقام المحمود ومحل الشفاعة خيرا مما أعطيتك في الدنيا من النبوة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p396/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p396/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p396/r4.claim: The clause is an independent continuation of the opening oath clauses, not its answer: after denying abandonment, it reassures that the Prophet's ending will surpass his beginning in this life and the next.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p396/r4.anchor: والجملة معطوفة على الجمل الابتدائية وليست معطوفة على جملة جواب القسم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p396/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p396/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p396/r5.claim: The definite forms al-ākhirah and al-ūlā generalize the statement into a concluding maxim that includes ongoing revelation and other forms of good.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p396/r5.anchor: وما في تعريف ( الآخرة ) و { الأولى } من التعميم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p396/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p396/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p396/r6.claim: The terms may denote the afterlife and worldly life, promising eternal good, while also describing the Prophet's circumstances as progressing from one state to a better one.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p396/r6.anchor: فيجوز أن يكون المراد هنا من كلا اللفظين كلا معنييه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p398/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p398/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p398/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhshari takes both lām particles as lām al-ibtidāʾ and supplies an omitted subject in the second clause: 'You will surely be given by your Lord.'
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p398/r1.anchor: جزم صاحب ( الكشاف ) بأنه لام الابتداء وقدر مبتدأ محذوفا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p157#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p157#2/r1.speaker: عطاء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p157#2/r1.claim: ʿAṭāʾ says the afterlife is better for the Prophet than this world.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p157#2/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى وللآخرة خير لك من الأولى قال عطاء خير لك من الدنيا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p157#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p157#2/r2.speaker: غيره
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p157#2/r2.claim: Another explanation says what the Prophet receives in the afterlife exceeds the honor bestowed on him in worldly life.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p157#2/r2.anchor: وقال غيره الذي لك في الآخرة أعظم مما أعطاك من كرامة الدنيا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p771/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p771/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p771/r1.claim: Denying abandonment implies continuing revelation and God's love, yet the Prophet's standing in the afterlife will surpass even this honor.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p771/r1.anchor: لما كان في ضمن نفي التوديع والقلي : أن الله مواصلك بالوحي إليك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p771/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p771/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p771/r2.claim: The hereafter brings precedence over all prophets, testimony by the Prophet's community, raised believer ranks through his intercession, and other honors.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p771/r2.anchor: وهو السبق والتقدم على جميع أنبياء الله ورسله ، وشهادة أمته

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p293/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p293/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p293/r1.claim: He reports that the Prophet was shown the conquests his community would make and rejoiced, after which this verse was revealed.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p293/r1.anchor: روى ابن عباس قال : عرض على رسول الله

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p293/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p293/r2.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p293/r2.claim: He says the afterlife is better for the Prophet than what delighted him in worldly life.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p293/r2.anchor: أعجبك في الدنيا , قاله يحيى بن سلام

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p293/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p293/r3.speaker: ابن شجرة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p293/r3.claim: He says the Prophet's ultimate return to God will be greater than the worldly honor already given him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p293/r3.anchor: من كرامة الدنيا , قاله ابن شجرة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p345/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p345/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p345/r1.claim: The afterlife's honored station, Pool, and promised good are better than what pleased the Prophet in worldly life; alternatively, the verse expands the reassurance that God continues revelation and loves him, promising an even greater afterlife rank.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p345/r1.anchor: ما أعد الله لك فى الآخرة من المقام المحمود والحوض المورود والخير الموعود خير مما أعجبك فى الدنيا

QURTUBI-FULL:93:4-5/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:4-5/r1.speaker: ابن إسحاق
QURTUBI-FULL:93:4-5/r1.claim: Ibn Ishaq says the better afterlife is what awaits Muhammad on returning to God, better than prompt worldly honors.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:4-5/r1.anchor: روى مسلمة عن ابن إسحاق قال: { وللآخرة خير لك من الأولى } أي ما عندي في مرجعك

QURTUBI-FULL:93:4-5/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:4-5/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:93:4-5/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Prophet saw future conquests of his community and rejoiced, so Gabriel brought the promise of the afterlife and God’s gift.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:4-5/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: أري النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ما يفتح الله على أمته بعده فسر بذلك فنزل جبريل بقوله

QURTUBI-FULL:93:4-5/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:4-5/r3.speaker: ابن إسحاق
QURTUBI-FULL:93:4-5/r3.claim: Ibn Ishaq glosses the promise as victory in this world and reward in the afterlife.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:4-5/r3.anchor: قال ابن إسحاق: الفلج في الدنيا، والثواب في الآخرة

QUTB-ZILAL:93:4/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:93:4/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:93:4/r1.claim: God's stream of favor never dries up: the Prophet will receive better goodness from God in the hereafter than in worldly life, for God is goodness in both.
QUTB-ZILAL:93:4/r1.anchor: فإن لك عنده في الآخرة من الحسنى خيرا مما يعطيك منها في الدنيا

RAZI-FULL:v31p191#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p191#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p191#2/r1.claim: Cessation of revelation need not mean removal from prophethood; it could signal that the mission is complete and death near, which is good because the Prophet's afterlife portion is better.
RAZI-FULL:v31p191#2/r1.anchor: انقطاع الوحي لا يجوز أن يكون لأنه عزل عن النبوة

RAZI-FULL:v31p191#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p191#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p191#2/r2.claim: Because 'your Lord has not abandoned you' conferred great honor, the next verse assures the Prophet that his afterlife portion with God will be greater still.
RAZI-FULL:v31p191#2/r2.anchor: لما نزل : { ما ودعك ربك } ( الضحى : 3 ) حصل له بهذا تشريف عظيم

RAZI-FULL:v31p191#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p191#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p191#2/r3.claim: Razi also suggests future conditions will surpass past ones, with God increasing the Prophet's honor and rank day by day.
RAZI-FULL:v31p191#2/r3.anchor: ما يخطر / ببالي ، وهو أن يكون المعنى وللأحوال الآتية خير لك من الماضية

RAZI-FULL:v31p191#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p191#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p191#2/r4.claim: The afterlife is better because God there does what He wills, whereas the Prophet can do what he wants in worldly life.
RAZI-FULL:v31p191#2/r4.anchor: كأنه تعالى يقول له إنك في الدنيا على خير لأنك تفعل فيها ما تريد

RAZI-FULL:v31p191#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p191#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p191#2/r5.claim: His nation will join him in Paradise like children joining a father; the Qur'an calls his wives believers' mothers and his descendants a delight of the eyes.
RAZI-FULL:v31p191#2/r5.anchor: الآخرة خير لك يجتمع عندك أمتك إذ الأمة له كالأولاد

RAZI-FULL:v31p191#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p191#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p191#2/r6.claim: The afterlife is his possession while this world is not; even if it were lesser, what he owns is better than what he does not, and in reality it is far superior.
RAZI-FULL:v31p191#2/r6.anchor: الآخرة خير لك لأنك اشتريتها ، أما هذه ليست لك

RAZI-FULL:v31p191#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p191#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p191#2/r7.claim: In this world disbelievers taunt him, but in the next his nation witnesses over other nations and he over prophets, with God testifying for him.
RAZI-FULL:v31p191#2/r7.anchor: في الدنيا الكفار يطعنون فيك أما في الآخرة فأجعل أمتك شهداء على الأمم

RAZI-FULL:v31p191#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p191#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p191#2/r8.claim: Worldly delights are few, tainted, and fleeting, whereas afterlife delights are many, pure, and everlasting.
RAZI-FULL:v31p191#2/r8.anchor: أن خيرات الدنيا قليلة مشوبة منقطعة

RAZI-FULL:v31p192/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p192/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p192/r1.claim: The promise says 'for you' rather than 'for you all' because some companions' afterlife may be worse; universalizing it would be false, while naming only the obedient exposes sinners and hypocrites.
RAZI-FULL:v31p192/r1.anchor: لأنه كان في جماعته من كانت الآخرة شرا له

RAZI-FULL:v31p192/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p192/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p192/r2.claim: Moses said his Lord was with him and would guide him, while Muhammad said God was with 'us,' since only a prophet and the certainly blessed Abu Bakr accompanied him.
RAZI-FULL:v31p192/r2.anchor: ولهذا السبب قال موسى عليه السلام : { كلا إن معى ربى سيهدين }

RAZI-FULL:v31p192/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p192/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p192/r3.claim: A report says Moses led thousands in three days of rain supplication, withheld because a backbiter was among them; after God revealed that man had died, Moses found seventy biers at the prayer ground.
RAZI-FULL:v31p192/r3.anchor: وروي أن موسى عليه السلام خرج للاستسقاء ، ومعه الألوف ثلاثة أيام

RAZI-FULL:v31p192/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p192/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p192/r4.claim: The saying about crouched elders hints at this community's special favor: God rejected thousands because of one sinner but pardons sinners because of one obedient person.
RAZI-FULL:v31p192/r4.anchor: عليه السلام قال : ( لولا شيوخ ركع ) وفيه إشارة إلى زيادة فضيلة هذه الأمة

SAMIN-DURR:93:4/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:93:4/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:93:4/r1.claim: The lām on wa-la-l-ākhirah is the oath's answer: God swears by four matters, two denials of abandonment and hatred, then the afterlife's superiority and a promise to give satisfaction.
SAMIN-DURR:93:4/r1.anchor: الظاهر في هذه اللام أنها جواب القسم، وكذلك في " ولسوف " أقسم تعالى على أربعة أشياء

SAMIN-DURR:93:4/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:93:4/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:93:4/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī takes the lām before sawfa as lām of emphasis, supplying a hidden subject, because an oath-lām before a present verb ordinarily requires the emphatic nūn.
SAMIN-DURR:93:4/r2.anchor: هي لام الابتداء المؤكدة لمضمون الجملة، والمبتدأ محذوف تقديره: ولأنت سوف يعطيك

SAMIN-DURR:93:4/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:93:4/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:93:4/r3.claim: The author chooses the oath-lām account, noting the grammar allows omission of emphatic nūn when an interval such as sawfa or a verb object intervenes.

SAMIN-DURR:93:4/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:93:4/r4.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
SAMIN-DURR:93:4/r4.claim: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī says this is the lām of an oath such as la-aqūman, not the lām in inna Zaydan la-qāʾim; sawfa substitutes for one emphatic nūn.
SAMIN-DURR:93:4/r4.anchor: قال الفارسي: " ليست هذه اللام هي التي في قولك:

SAMIN-DURR:93:4/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:93:4/r5.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:93:4/r5.claim: The interlocutor first calls the lām on wa-la-l-ākhirah an emphatic lām of beginning, then allows it and the lām on wa-la-sawfa to be oath-lāms coordinated with the oath's answer.
SAMIN-DURR:93:4/r5.anchor: ويجوز عندي أن تكون اللام في " وللآخرة خير " وفي " ولسوف يعطيك " اللام التي يتلقى بها القسم

SAMIN-DURR:93:4/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:93:4/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:93:4/r6.claim: The author says the lām clauses clearly continue the oath answer; a hidden subject after al-Zamakhsharī's analysis does not prevent that function.
SAMIN-DURR:93:4/r6.anchor: ولا يظهر انقطاع هذه الجملة عن جواب القسم البتة، وكذلك في { ولسوف

STUDYQURAN:93:4/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:93:4/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:93:4/r1.claim: The wording literally says the last is better than the first; Quranic teaching generally makes the Hereafter better than worldly life, which is fleeting enjoyment.
STUDYQURAN:93:4/r1.anchor: This verse literally reads, “And the last shall be better for thee than the first.” Throughout the Quran the Abode of the Hereafter is considered better

STUDYQURAN:93:4/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:93:4/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:93:4/r2.claim: The Quran condemns those who trade away the Hereafter for worldly life.
STUDYQURAN:93:4/r2.anchor: The Quran thus criticizes those who have purchased the world at the price of the Hereafter

STUDYQURAN:93:4/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:93:4/r3.speaker: Prophet
STUDYQURAN:93:4/r3.claim: A report says the Prophet chose to be with God in the Hereafter rather than remain in this life until its end and then enter Paradise.
STUDYQURAN:93:4/r3.anchor: It is reported that when the Prophet was given the choice between remaining in this life until the end of time

TAB:93:4/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:93:4/r1.speaker: author
TAB:93:4/r1.claim: The Hereafter and what God has prepared for Muhammad there are better than this world's life and what it contains; therefore he should not grieve what passed.
TAB:93:4/r1.anchor: وللدار الاَخرة ،   وما أعدّ الله لك فيها ،   خير لك من الدار الدنيا وما فيها يقول :  فلا تخزن على ما فاتك منها

TABRISI:93:5#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:93:5#2/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:93:5#2/r5.claim: The coming Hereafter and its lasting reward are better for the Prophet than the transient worldly life.
TABRISI:93:5#2/r5.anchor: ثواب الآخرة والنعيم الدائم فيها خير لك من الدنيا الفانية

TABRISI:93:5#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:93:5#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:93:5#2/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that the Prophet will have a million pearl palaces in Paradise, with all desired spouses and attendants.
TABRISI:93:5#2/r6.anchor: له صلى الله عليه وسلم في الجنة ألف ألف قصر من اللؤلؤ

TABRISI:93:5#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:93:5#2/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:93:5#2/r7.claim: Alternatively, the remainder of the Prophet's lifetime is better than its beginning because victories and success will come.
TABRISI:93:5#2/r7.anchor: ولآخر عمرك الذي بقي خير لك من أوله لما يكون فيه من الفتوح والنصرة

TABRISI:93:10-11/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:93:10-11/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:93:10-11/r12.claim: The promise that the Hereafter is better connects to the preceding reassurance of God's love and gifts: revelation and love endure, and the Prophet's future rank exceeds today's gifts; the connection from finding him needy to recounting favors joins gifts to their Giver and promises future favor as in the past.
TABRISI:93:10-11/r12.anchor: إثباتا لمحبته سبحانه إياه وإنعامه عليه فاتصل هذا أيضا به

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p106/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p106/r1.speaker: عطاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p106/r1.claim: The Hereafter means Paradise, which is better for the Prophet than this world; Muqātil gives the same interpretation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p106/r1.anchor: قال عطاء (¬2)، ومقاتل (¬3): يريد والجنة (¬4) خير لك من الدنيا.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p106/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p106/r2.speaker: علي بن عبد الله بن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p106/r2.claim: The Prophet was shown what would be opened for his community after him and was comforted by it; then this verse was revealed.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p106/r2.anchor: وقال علي بن عبد الله بن عباس: أري رسول الله -صلى الله عليه وسلم- ما يفتح على أمته من بعده

WAHIDI-QT:93:4/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:93:4/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:93:4/r1.claim: The Hereafter is better for Muhammad because God will grant him honors and ranks there.
WAHIDI-QT:93:4/r1.anchor: { وللآخرة خير لك من الأولى } لأن الله يعطيك فيها الكرامات والدرجات

CORPUSCORANICUM:93:4:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:93:4:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:93:4:anmerkung/r1.claim: Al-ūlā here is ‘this world’ as the early-Makkan opposite of al-ākhira; other suras use al-ḥayāt al-dunyā, ‘life below.’
CORPUSCORANICUM:93:4:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Als Gegenbegriff zu al-ʾāḫira findet sich in frühmekkanischer Zeit entweder wie hier al-ʾūlā, „das Diesseits“

CORPUSCORANICUM:93:4:anmerkung/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:93:4:anmerkung/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:93:4:anmerkung/r2.claim: The paired worldly and coming-world concepts resemble Jewish-Christian usage; poetry already knows dunyā and may distinguish it from their afterlife beliefs, while the Quran asserts the afterlife’s superiority against poetry.
CORPUSCORANICUM:93:4:anmerkung/r2.anchor: Möglicherweise setzt sich der poetische dunyā-Diskurs also bewusst und terminologisch pointiert von jüdisch-christlichen Jenseitsvorstellungen ab

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:93:4/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:93:4/r1.speaker: Birinci yorum
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:93:4/r1.claim: One reading says the Prophet's coming life, especially the later phase of his prophetic mission, will be better and more successful than its beginning.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:93:4/r1.anchor: bundan sonraki hayatın bundan önceki hayatından daha güzel ve başarılı olacak

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:93:4/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:93:4/r2.speaker: İkinci yorum
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:93:4/r2.claim: Another reading takes the Hereafter's eternal life in Paradise to be better than the temporary life of this world.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:93:4/r2.anchor: Ebedî olan âhirette cennetteki hayatın geçici olan dünya hayatından daha güzel olacak

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:93:4/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:93:4/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:93:4/r3.claim: The author prefers the first reading: against claims that revelation had stopped and Muhammad's cause would fail, God promises his future prophetic work will be spiritually and practically more fruitful.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:93:4/r3.anchor: bundan sonraki hayatının, peygamberlik faaliyetlerinin ruhanî tekâmülünün öncekinden daha verimli, daha başarılı olacağını müjdelemiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:93:4/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:93:4/r4.speaker: Putperestler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:93:4/r4.claim: The idolaters said revelation no longer came to Muhammad and God had forgotten him, hoping his mission would end in failure.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:93:4/r4.anchor: “Artık Muhammed’e vahiy gelmiyor; Allah onu unuttu” gibi sözler söyleyerek

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p231/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p231/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p231/r1.claim: The Prophet was shown what would be opened to his community after him and rejoiced, so the statement that the Hereafter is better than the first life was revealed; al-Tabarani's chain is graded good.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p231/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عرض علي ما هو مفتوح لأمتي بعدي فسرني فأنزل الله

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p458/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p458/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p458/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet rejoiced when shown his community's future conquests, so these verses were revealed; he was promised a thousand pearl palaces in Paradise, each with its provisions of spouses and servants.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p458/r1.anchor: علي بن عبد الله بن عباس، عن أبيه قال: رأى رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - ما يفتح على أمته

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p412/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p412/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p412/r1.claim: The afterlife is set against what came before: what lies ahead for the Prophet is better than his past, and the prefixed lām emphasizes this promise.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p412/r1.anchor: ما يأتي خير لك أيها الرسول مما مضى

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p412/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p412/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p412/r2.claim: Saying ‘than the world’ would limit the promise to the afterlife and deny that the Prophet’s remaining life would bring better things; the verse also confirms the preceding reassurance.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p412/r2.anchor: وهذه الآية توكيد لما سبقها في قوله تعالى ما ودعك ربك وما قلى

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p412/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p412/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p412/r3.claim: The phrase specifies ‘for you’ because this sūra and al-Sharḥ address the Prophet; making the promise universal would fail for some people whose afterlife is worse than their worldly life.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p412/r3.anchor: قال تعالى (وللآخرة خير لك من الأولى)

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p415/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p415/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p415/r1.claim: The sūra moves from darkness to light—orphanship to shelter, lostness to guidance, and need to wealth—in keeping with the claim that what comes later is better.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p415/r1.anchor: بدأ سبحانه وتعالى بالظلمة ثم النور

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p496/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p496/r1.speaker: ابن إسحاق
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p496/r1.claim: Ibn Isḥāq and others take “the latter is better” to mean the two abodes, this world and the next.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p496/r1.anchor: وللآخرة خير لك من الأولى: يريد الدارين، قاله ابن إسحاق وغيره.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p496/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p496/r2.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p496/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya allows that the verse may contrast the Prophet’s circumstances before and after the sūra, promising victory and success.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p496/r2.anchor: ويحتمل أن يريد حالتيه قبل نزول السورة وبعدها، وعده تعالى بالنصر والظفر،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p496/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p496/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p496/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī links the verse to the preceding denial of abandonment: God continues to reveal to and honor His beloved, then promises greater honors in the Hereafter, including precedence, testimony, elevated ranks, and intercession.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p496/r3.anchor: لما كان في ضمن نفي التوديع والقلى أن الله مواصلك بالوحي إليك

ALUSI-FULL:v30p158/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p158/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p158/r1.claim: The Hereafter is enduring and wholly free of worldly troubles, while the present life is transient and mixed with harm; even the Prophet's great worldly honor came with difficulties in administering affairs.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p158/r1.anchor: لما أنها باقية صافية عن الشوائب على الإطلاق وهذه فانية مشوبة بالمضار وما أوتي عليه الصلاة والسلام من شرف النبوة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p158/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p158/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p158/r2.claim: His afterlife honors—precedence over all prophets, his community's witness over others, and believers' elevation through his intercession—vastly surpass worldly beginnings.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p158/r2.anchor: من السبق والتقدم على كافة الأنبياء والرسل عليهم الصلاة والسلام يوم الجمع يوم يقوم الناس لرب العالمين

ALUSI-FULL:v30p158/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p158/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p158/r3.claim: The possessive exclusivity may contrast the Prophet's better Hereafter with those who mocked him over the pause in revelation, or it may include all the saved; the exclusivity is not necessarily restrictive.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p158/r3.anchor: قيل إضافي على معنى اختصاصه عليه الصلاة والسلام بخيرية الآخرة دون من أذاه وشمت بتأخير الوحي عنه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p158/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p158/r4.speaker: أبو إسحاق
ALUSI-FULL:v30p158/r4.claim: The apparent and transmitted interpretation from Abū Isḥāq takes the Hereafter and the first life as the afterlife and this world; Ibn ʿAṭiyya and others allow the end and beginning of the Prophet's career instead.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p158/r4.anchor: وحمل الآخرة على الدار الآخرة المقابلة للدنيا والأولى على الدار الأولى وهي الدنيا هو الظاهر المروي عن أبي إسحاق

ALUSI-FULL:v30p158/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p158/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v30p158/r5.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās says that the Prophet was shown the conquests his community would make after him, was pleased, and this verse was revealed; Alusi finds that wording especially clear for the worldly/afterlife interpretation.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p158/r5.anchor: أخرج الطبراني في الأوسط والبيهقي في الدلائل عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما قال قال رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم عرض على ما هو مفتوح لأمتي

ALUSI-FULL:v30p158/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p158/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p158/r6.claim: A less persuasive proposal says the pause in revelation signaled that the Prophet's death was near, and death was better because of his afterlife reward; the straightforward reading is an independent statement linked to what came before.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p158/r6.anchor: وجوز أيضا أن يكون المعنى أن انقطاع الوحي لا يجوز أن يكون لما يتوهمون لأنه عز عن النبوة وهو مستحيل في الحكمة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p159#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p159#2/r2.speaker: عصام الدين
ALUSI-FULL:v30p159#2/r2.claim: ʿIṣām al-Dīn takes the preceding denial as circumstantial: the Hereafter is better for the Prophet, so his Lord would not abandon him; the promise then means He will give him the Hereafter. Alusi objects that the paired laams and oath make this reading unlikely and its paraphrase is strained.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p159#2/r2.anchor: الأظهر أن جملة ما ودعك حالية أي ما ودعك ربك وما قلاك والحال أن الآخرة خير لك من الأولى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p454#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p454#2/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p454#2/r1.claim: The Prophet said that God chose the afterlife over this world for his household.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p454#2/r1.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "إنا أهل بيت اختار الله لنا الآخرة على الدنيا

BAYDAWI-FULL:93:4-5/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:93:4-5/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:93:4-5/r1.claim: The afterlife is enduring and free of worldly defects, whereas this life passes and is mixed with harms; the Prophet's final state will exceed his beginning.
BAYDAWI-FULL:93:4-5/r1.anchor: فإنها باقية خالصة عن الشوائب وهذه فانية مشوبة بالمضار

BAYDAWI-FULL:93:4-5/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:93:4-5/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:93:4-5/r2.claim: After promising continuing revelation and honor in this life, God promises the Prophet an even greater afterlife gift, including perfection, triumph, and elevation of the religion.
BAYDAWI-FULL:93:4-5/r2.anchor: وعد له ما هو أعلى وأجل من ذلك في الآخرة

BINTSHATI:v1p36/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p36/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p36/r1.claim: The surah is among the earliest revelations and came in Mecca years before the Hijra.
BINTSHATI:v1p36/r1.anchor: وسورة الضحى من أوائل الوحي، نزلت بمكة قبل الهجرة بسنين

BINTSHATI:v1p36/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p36/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p36/r2.claim: The apparent pause in revelation was natural, like night settling after the dawn's brightness.
BINTSHATI:v1p36/r2.anchor: أن فتور الوحي ظاهرة طبيعية، شأنها شأن سجو الليل بعد إشراق الضحى

BINTSHATI:v1p36/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p36/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p36/r3.claim: The Quran gives neither a cause nor duration for the pause; proposed explanations and counts of twelve to forty days add nothing to its central meaning.
BINTSHATI:v1p36/r3.anchor: فلأن الذي يعنيه هو جوهر الموقف لا تفصيلاته الجزئية

BINTSHATI:v1p36/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p36/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p36/r4.claim: Al-ākhirah broadly means what comes later, the end or outcome in this life or the next; here it most likely means Muhammad's hoped-for future.
BINTSHATI:v1p36/r4.anchor: وفي آية الضحى، يرجع أن الآخرة هي الغد المرجو، مجيئها مع {لَكَ} خاصة بمحمد

BINTSHATI:v1p36/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p36/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p36/r5.claim: The promised good confirms that God has not abandoned or hated the Prophet and comforts him after the pause.
BINTSHATI:v1p36/r5.anchor: وقد أكد الله بهذا الخير الموعود، نفى التوديع والقلى، ليذهب عن رسوله أثر فتور الوحي

BIQAI-FULL:v8p455#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p455#2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p455#2/r1.claim: The surah was revealed after a pause in revelation when disbelievers said God had abandoned Muḥammad; it announces favor and glad tidings.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p455#2/r1.anchor: كان قد فتر عنه الوحي حتى قال بعض الكفار : قلى محمدا ربه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p455#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p455#2/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p455#2/r2.claim: Anas reports that the Prophet said he was shown the successive gifts that would be opened to his community after him, and this pleased him.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p455#2/r2.anchor: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( أريت ما هو مفتوح على أمتي

BIQAI-FULL:v8p455#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p455#2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p455#2/r3.claim: The Hereafter is better for the Prophet than the first life and implies his continual ascent from one high state to a higher one without end.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p455#2/r3.anchor: التي هي المقصود من الوجود بالذات لأنها باقية خالصة عن شوائب الكدر

BIQAI-FULL:v8p455#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p455#2/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p455#2/r4.claim: People fall into four worldly and afterlife patterns: obedient rich prosper in both, poor unbelievers fare badly in both, wealthy unbelievers have only worldly good, and poor believers only afterlife good.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p455#2/r4.anchor: منهم من له الخير في الدارين وهم أهل الطاعة الأغنياء

ABUHAYYAN:93:4/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:93:4/r1.speaker: ابن إسحاق وغيره
ABUHAYYAN:93:4/r1.claim: Ibn Isḥāq and others say the two terms refer to the two abodes, this world and the next.
ABUHAYYAN:93:4/r1.anchor: يريد الدارين ،   قاله ابن إسحاق وغيره

ABUHAYYAN:93:4/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:93:4/r2.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN:93:4/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyyah suggests they may be the Prophet's states before and after the sūra, with a promise of victory and triumph.
ABUHAYYAN:93:4/r2.anchor: وعده تعالى بالنصر والظفر ،   قاله ابن عطية اهتمالاً

ABUHAYYAN:93:4/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:93:4/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN:93:4/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī links this to the preceding denial of abandonment: continued revelation and God's love are supreme honor, so the Prophet's afterlife will be greater, with precedence over prophets, his community's witness, and intercession raising believers' ranks.
ABUHAYYAN:93:4/r3.anchor: وقال الزمخشري : فإن قلت : كيف اتصل قوله

ALUSI:93:4/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:93:4/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:93:4/r1.claim: The afterlife is better because it is everlasting and wholly free of worldly defects; even prophetic distinction in this life has incidental hindrances, while the afterlife brings precedence, the praiseworthy station, the community's witness, and believers' elevation through his intercession.
ALUSI:93:4/r1.anchor: لما أنها باقية صافية عن الشوائب على الإطلاق وهذه فانية مشوبة بالمضار

ALUSI:93:4/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:93:4/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI:93:4/r2.claim: The afterlife gifts prepared for him include precedence over all prophets and messengers, the praiseworthy station, his community witnessing for other nations, and believers raised through his intercession.
ALUSI:93:4/r2.anchor: عندما أعد له عليه الصلاة والسلام في الآخرة من السبق والتقدم على كافة الأنبياء والرسل عليهم الصلاة والسلام يوم الجمع

ALUSI:93:4/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:93:4/r3.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:93:4/r3.claim: The lām may mark a relative distinction: the afterlife's goodness is particular to the Prophet rather than those who harmed him and mocked the revelation delay.
ALUSI:93:4/r3.anchor: والاختصاص الذي تقتضيه اللام قيل إضافي على معنى اختصاصه عليه الصلاة والسلام بخيرية الآخرة دون من آذاه وشمت

ALUSI:93:4/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:93:4/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI:93:4/r4.claim: The lām need not restrict the promise to the Prophet alone: all successful people share in afterlife good, though his reward is necessarily greater and the praiseworthy station uniquely his.
ALUSI:93:4/r4.anchor: ولا مانع من عمومه لجميع الفائزين كيف وقد علم بالضرورة أن الخير المعد له عليه الصلاة والسلام خير من المعد لغيره

ALUSI:93:4/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:93:4/r5.speaker: أبو إسحاق وغيره
ALUSI:93:4/r5.claim: The apparent and transmitted meaning takes the Afterlife and the First as the next life and this worldly life, respectively.
ALUSI:93:4/r5.anchor: وحمل الآخرة على الدار الآخرة المقابلة للدنيا والأولى على الدار الأولى وهي الدنيا هو الظاهر المروى عن أبي إسحق وغيره

ALUSI:93:4/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:93:4/r6.speaker: ابن عطية وجماعة
ALUSI:93:4/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya and others allow the terms to mean the end and beginning of the Prophet's mission: its ending will steadily grow stronger and higher.
ALUSI:93:4/r6.anchor: وقال ابن عطية وجماعة يحتمل أن يراد بهما نهاية أمره صلى الله عليه وسلم وبدايته

ALUSI:93:4/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:93:4/r7.speaker: ابن عطية وجماعة
ALUSI:93:4/r7.claim: On the beginning-and-end interpretation, the definite articles refer back or stand in place of a possessive construction.
ALUSI:93:4/r7.anchor: فاللام فيهما للعهد أو عوض عن المضاف إليه أي لنهاية أمرك خير من بدايته

ALUSI:93:4/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:93:4/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI:93:4/r8.claim: A marfūʿ report from Ibn ʿAbbās says the Prophet was shown what would be opened for his community after him and rejoiced; the verse was then revealed, supporting the afterlife reading.
ALUSI:93:4/r8.anchor: أخرج الطبراني في «الأوسط » والبيهقي في «الدلائل » عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما

ALUSI:93:4/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:93:4/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI:93:4/r9.claim: Al-Ālūsī prefers linking the promise to the preceding denial: after the assurance that God had not abandoned him, the Prophet is told that his future reward exceeds the honor already given.
ALUSI:93:4/r9.anchor: ثم أن ربط الآية بما قبلها على الوجه الذي سمعت هو ما اختاره غير واحد من الأجلة

ALUSI:93:4/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:93:4/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI:93:4/r10.claim: One proposed link says that, after the denial itself bestowed great honor, God reassured the Prophet that this honor is surpassed by what awaits him in the afterlife.
ALUSI:93:4/r10.anchor: وجوز أن يقال فيه أنه لما نزل { ما ودعك ربك وما قلى }

ALUSI:93:4/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:93:4/r11.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:93:4/r11.claim: A weaker proposal says that if revelation ceased, it would signal death rather than dismissal from prophethood, and death would be better because his afterlife reward exceeds this world's.
ALUSI:93:4/r11.anchor: وجوز أيضاً أن يكون المعنى إنقطاع الوحي لا يجوز أن يكون لما يتوهمون لأنه عزل عن النبوة وهو مستحيل في الحكمة

ALUSI:93:4/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:93:4/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI:93:4/r12.claim: Al-Ālūsī judges the death-and-revelation-cessation proposal much weaker than the preceding explanation.
ALUSI:93:4/r12.anchor: وهذا كما ترى دون ما قبله بكثير

BAGHAWI:93:4/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:93:4/r1.speaker: عبد الله
BAGHAWI:93:4/r1.claim: Ibn Masʿud reports the Prophet saying that God chose the Hereafter over this world for his household.
BAGHAWI:93:4/r1.anchor: عن عبد الله قال : " قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : إنا أهل بيت اختار الله لنا الآخرة على الدنيا

BAYDAWI:93:4/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:93:4/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:93:4/r1.claim: Revelation reportedly paused for several days because the Prophet omitted an exception formula as in al-Kahf, rebuked a persistent questioner, a dead puppy lay beneath his bed, or for another reason; polytheists said his Lord had abandoned and hated him, and the sūra answered them.
BAYDAWI:93:4/r1.anchor: روي أن الوحي تأخر عنه أياما لتركه الاستثناء كما مر في سورة الكهف أو لزجره سائلا ملحا أو لأن جروا ميتا

BAYDAWI:93:4/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:93:4/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:93:4/r2.claim: The Hereafter is enduring and free of the defects that mix into transient worldly life.
BAYDAWI:93:4/r2.anchor: فإنها باقية خالصة عن الشوائب وهذه فانية مشوبة بالمضار

BAYDAWI:93:4/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:93:4/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:93:4/r3.claim: Since God continues to favor him with revelation and honor in this life, He promises him something higher in the Hereafter; alternatively, the end of his course is better than its beginning as his rank keeps rising.
BAYDAWI:93:4/r3.anchor: كأنه لما بين أنه سبحانه وتعالى لا يزال يواصله بالوحي والكرامة في الدنيا وعد له ما هو أعلى وأجل من ذلك في الآخرة أو لنهاية أمرك خير من بدايته

BIQAI:93:4/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:93:4/r1.speaker: أنس
BIQAI:93:4/r1.claim: Anas reports hearing the Prophet say that he was delighted by what would be opened for his community after him, land after land.
BIQAI:93:4/r1.anchor: روي عن أنس رضي الله عنه أنه قال : سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول :

BIQAI:93:4/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:93:4/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:93:4/r2.claim: The hereafter is the higher and greater realm: even its lowest entrant receives what no eye has seen, ear heard, or heart imagined, so the Prophet's share is beyond comparison.
BIQAI:93:4/r2.anchor: ولأدنى من يدخلها فيها ما لا عين رأت ولا أذن سمعت ولا خطر على قلب بشر

BIQAI:93:4/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:93:4/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:93:4/r3.claim: Al-ākhirah can mean the lasting, untroubled hereafter, the true end of existence, or the Prophet's later condition; the latter sense implies endless ascent from one perfection to another.
BIQAI:93:4/r3.anchor: أي التي هي المقصود من الوجود بالذات لأنها باقية خالصة عن شوائب الكدر أو الحالة المتأخرة لك

BIQAI:93:4/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:93:4/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI:93:4/r4.claim: The qualification “for you” matters because this upward progression is not true of everyone; the fleeting world offers no unalloyed joy and is less noble than what follows.
BIQAI:93:4/r4.anchor: الدنيا الفانية التي لا سرور فيها خالص كما أن النهار الذي هو بعد الليل خير منه وأشرف ولا سيما الضحى منه

BIQAI:93:4/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:93:4/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI:93:4/r5.claim: People fall into four groups: obedient wealthy people have good in both realms; poor unbelievers bad in both; wealthy unbelievers apparent worldly good but afterlife harm; poor believers worldly hardship but afterlife good. He illustrates this with a four-part poem.
BIQAI:93:4/r5.anchor: وقد أفهم ذلك أن الناس على أربعة أقسام : منهم من له الخير في الدارين وهم أهل الطاعة الأغنياء

DURR:93:4/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:93:4/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR:93:4/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that a vision of the future conquests opened to the Prophet’s community made him glad, and this verse was revealed.
DURR:93:4/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : «عرض علي ما هو مفتوح لأمتي بعدي فسرني

DURR:93:4/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:93:4/r2.speaker: عكرمة
DURR:93:4/r2.claim: Ikrimah says that when the verse was revealed, al-Abbas understood it to mean God would leave His Prophet among them only briefly because something better awaited him.
DURR:93:4/r2.anchor: عن عكرمة رضي الله عنه قال : لما نزلت { وللآخرة خير لك من الأولى } قال العباس بن عبد المطلب

IBNASHUR:93:4/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:93:4/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:93:4/r1.claim: The sentence coordinates with the opening oath phrase, not its answer; it is an independent assertion that follows the denial with glad tidings.
IBNASHUR:93:4/r1.anchor: عطف على جملة :  { والضحى } [ الضحى : 1 ] فهو كلام مبتدأ به

IBNASHUR:93:4/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:93:4/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:93:4/r2.claim: His later outcome is better than his beginning, and God will conclude his affairs with what surpasses what He has already given him in this life and the next.
IBNASHUR:93:4/r2.anchor: فلما نُفي القِلى بشّر بأن آخرته خير من أولاه ،  وأن عاقبته أحسن من بدأته

IBNASHUR:93:4/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:93:4/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:93:4/r3.claim: The generic definite nouns make this a comprehensive closing statement that includes the continuation of revelation and every other good.
IBNASHUR:93:4/r3.anchor: وما في تعريف « الآخرة » و { الأولى } من التعميم يجعل معنى هذه الجملة في معنى التذييل الشامل لاستمرار الوحي

IBNASHUR:93:4/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:93:4/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:93:4/r4.claim: Both terms may denote the afterlife and worldly life, promising eternal good and an earthly course that moves from one state to a better one.
IBNASHUR:93:4/r4.anchor: فيجوز أن يكون المراد هنا من كلا اللفظين كلا معنييه فيفيد أن الحياة الآخرة خير له من هذه الحياة العاجلة

IBNASHUR:93:4/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:93:4/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:93:4/r5.claim: The renewed revelation is better than the previous return, intimating God's guarantee that revelation will not cease again.
IBNASHUR:93:4/r5.anchor: ويومىء ذلك إلى أن عودة نزول الوحي عليه هذه المرة خير من العودة التي سبقت ، أي تكفل الله بأن لا ينقطع عنه نزول الوحي

IBNASHUR:93:4/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:93:4/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:93:4/r6.claim: The lam on al-akhirah and al-ula is generic: every later or deferred matter is better than its immediate counterpart in this world and the next.
IBNASHUR:93:4/r6.anchor: فاللام في « الآخرة » و { الأولى } لام الجنس ،  أي كل آجل أمره هو خير من عاجله في هذه الدنيا

IBNASHUR:93:4/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:93:4/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:93:4/r7.claim: The lam in laka marks اختصاص: the promise covers all connected to the Prophet personally, his religion, and his community, including Islam's spread and the community's hoped-for good.
IBNASHUR:93:4/r7.anchor: واللام في قوله :  { لك } لام الاختصاص ،  أي خير مختص بك وهو شامل لكل ما له تعلق بنفس النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNASHUR:93:4/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:93:4/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR:93:4/r8.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas says the Prophet was shown the conquests awaiting his community after him and was pleased, after which this verse was revealed; Ibn Ashur gives no grading here.
IBNASHUR:93:4/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال :   "  قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عُرض عليّ ما هو مفتوح لأمتي بعدي

IBNATIYYA:93:4/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:93:4/r1.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNATIYYA:93:4/r1.claim: Ibn Isḥāq and others understand the two terms as the afterlife and worldly life: the former is better for the Prophet.
IBNATIYYA:93:4/r1.anchor: يحتمل أن يريد الدارين الدنيا والآخرة ، وهذا تأويل ابن إسحاق وغيره

IBNATIYYA:93:4/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:93:4/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:93:4/r2.claim: Alternatively, the verse compares the Prophet's worldly condition before and after this sūra, promising victory and prominence; verse 5 may be read similarly.
IBNATIYYA:93:4/r2.anchor: ويحتمل أن يريد حاليه في الدنيا قبل نزول السورة وبعدها فوعده الله تعالى على هذا التأويل بالنصر والظهور ، وكذلك قوله تعالى : { ولسوف يعطيك ربك } الآية

IBNKATHIR:93:4/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:93:4/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:93:4/r1.claim: The Hereafter is better for the Prophet than this world, as shown by his exceptional asceticism and his choosing what is with God over worldly life when offered the choice near death.
IBNKATHIR:93:4/r1.anchor: أي : والدار الآخرة خير لك من هذه الدار . ولهذا كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أزهد الناس في الدنيا ،

IBNKATHIR:93:4/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:93:4/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNKATHIR:93:4/r2.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reports that after the Prophet's rough mat marked his side, he compared himself and the world to a rider who rests under a tree then leaves it; al-Tirmidhī graded the report ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ.
IBNKATHIR:93:4/r2.anchor: عن عبد الله - هو ابن مسعود - قال : اضطجع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على حصير ، فأثر في جنبه ، فلما استيقظ

KASHSHAF:93:4/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:93:4/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:93:4/r1.claim: The denial of abandonment and rejection implies continued revelation and God’s love; the afterlife brings greater honor, including precedence among prophets, the community’s testimony, raised believer ranks through the Prophet’s intercession, and other gifts.
KASHSHAF:93:4/r1.anchor: قلت : لما كان في ضمن نفي التوديع والقلي : أنّ الله مواصلك بالوحي إليك ، وأنك حبيب الله ولا ترى كرامة أعظم من ذلك

MAWARDI:93:4/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:93:4/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI:93:4/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that God showed the Prophet what would be opened for his community after him; he rejoiced, and this verse was revealed.
MAWARDI:93:4/r1.anchor: روى ابن عباس قال : عرض على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ما هو مفتوح على أمته من بعده

MAWARDI:93:4/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:93:4/r2.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
MAWARDI:93:4/r2.claim: The Hereafter is better for the Prophet than what impressed him in worldly life.
MAWARDI:93:4/r2.anchor: أحدهما : وللآخرة خير لك مما أعجبك في الدنيا ، قاله يحيى بن سلام

MAWARDI:93:4/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:93:4/r3.speaker: ابن شجرة
MAWARDI:93:4/r3.claim: The Prophet’s return to God and what awaits him there are greater than the honor given to him in worldly life.
MAWARDI:93:4/r3.anchor: الثاني : أن مآلك في مرجعك إلى الله تعالى أعظم مما أعطاك من كرامة الدنيا ، قاله ابن شجرة

NASAFI:93:4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:93:4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:93:4/r1.claim: What God has prepared for the Prophet in the afterlife—the praised station, promised pool, and other promised good—is better than worldly things that impressed him.
NASAFI:93:4/r1.anchor: أي ما أعد الله لك في الآخرة من المقام المحمود والحوض المورود والخير الموعود خير مما أعجبك في الدنيا

NASAFI:93:4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:93:4/r2.speaker: قيل
NASAFI:93:4/r2.claim: The verse connects to the previous one because God's continued revelation shows His love for the Prophet.
NASAFI:93:4/r2.anchor: وقيل : وجه اتصاله بما قبله أنه لما كان في ضمن نفي التوديع والقلى

NASAFI:93:4/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:93:4/r3.speaker: قيل
NASAFI:93:4/r3.claim: The Prophet's afterlife state is greater still, including precedence over the prophets and his community's witness over other communities.
NASAFI:93:4/r3.anchor: أخبره أن حاله في الآخرة أعظم من ذلك لتقدمه على الأنبياء وشهادة أمته على الأمم وغير ذلك

QURTUBI:93:4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:93:4/r1.speaker: ابن إسحاق
QURTUBI:93:4/r1.claim: Ibn Isḥāq says what awaits Muhammad in his return to God is better than the worldly honor granted him quickly.
QURTUBI:93:4/r1.anchor: روى سلمة عن ابن إسحاق قال : " وللآخرة خير لك من الأولى " أي ما عندي في مرجعك إلي يا محمد

QURTUBI:93:4/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:93:4/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI:93:4/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the Prophet was shown what God would open for his community after him and rejoiced; Gabriel then brought these promises.
QURTUBI:93:4/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عباس : أري النبي صلى اللّه عليه وسلم ما يفتح اللّه على أمته بعده ؛ فسر بذلك ؛ فنزل جبريل بقوله

QURTUBI:93:4/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:93:4/r3.speaker: ابن إسحاق
QURTUBI:93:4/r3.claim: Ibn Isḥāq glosses the promise as victory in this world and reward in the next.
QURTUBI:93:4/r3.anchor: قال ابن إسحاق : الفلج في الدنيا ، والثواب في الآخرة

QURTUBI:93:4/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:93:4/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI:93:4/r4.claim: An alternative explanation is the Pool and intercession.

QURTUBI:93:4/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:93:4/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI:93:4/r5.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās, raised by al-Awzāʿī, says the Prophet was shown his community's future and received a thousand musk-soil pearl palaces in Paradise, with suitable spouses and servants in each.
QURTUBI:93:4/r5.anchor: وعن ابن عباس : ألف قصر من لؤلؤ أبيض ترابه المسك . رفعه الأوزاعي

QURTUBI:93:5/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:93:5/r1.speaker: ابن إسحاق
QURTUBI:93:5/r1.claim: Ibn Isḥāq says what awaits Muhammad in his return to God is better than the worldly honor granted him quickly.
QURTUBI:93:5/r1.anchor: روى سلمة عن ابن إسحاق قال : " وللآخرة خير لك من الأولى " أي ما عندي في مرجعك إلي يا محمد

QURTUBI:93:5/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:93:5/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI:93:5/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the Prophet was shown what God would open for his community after him and rejoiced; Gabriel then brought these promises.
QURTUBI:93:5/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عباس : أري النبي صلى اللّه عليه وسلم ما يفتح اللّه على أمته بعده ؛ فسر بذلك ؛ فنزل جبريل بقوله

QURTUBI:93:5/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:93:5/r3.speaker: ابن إسحاق
QURTUBI:93:5/r3.claim: Ibn Isḥāq glosses the promise as victory in this world and reward in the next.
QURTUBI:93:5/r3.anchor: قال ابن إسحاق : الفلج في الدنيا ، والثواب في الآخرة

QURTUBI:93:5/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:93:5/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI:93:5/r4.claim: An alternative explanation is the Pool and intercession.

QURTUBI:93:5/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:93:5/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI:93:5/r5.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās, raised by al-Awzāʿī, says the Prophet was shown his community's future and received a thousand musk-soil pearl palaces in Paradise, with suitable spouses and servants in each.
QURTUBI:93:5/r5.anchor: وعن ابن عباس : ألف قصر من لؤلؤ أبيض ترابه المسك . رفعه الأوزاعي

RAZI:93:4/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:4/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:93:4/r1.claim: One connection to the preceding verse is that a revelation pause could signal not dismissal but death; death is better because the Prophet's state with God in the Hereafter surpasses his worldly state.
RAZI:93:4/r1.anchor: أن يكون المعنى أن انقطاع الوحي لا يجوز أن يكون

RAZI:93:4/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:4/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:93:4/r2.claim: Another connection is that after God honored him by denying abandonment, He assures him that his Hereafter standing will be greater still.

RAZI:93:4/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:4/r3.speaker: author
RAZI:93:4/r3.claim: Rāzī's own proposed reading takes ākhira and ūlā as later and earlier conditions: God will increase the Prophet in honor and rank day by day.
RAZI:93:4/r3.anchor: وهو أن يكون المعنى وللأحوال الآتية خير لك

RAZI:93:4/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:4/r4.speaker: author
RAZI:93:4/r4.claim: One reason the Hereafter is better is that worldly life lets the Prophet do what he wants, while in the Hereafter God does what He wants for him.
RAZI:93:4/r4.anchor: إنك في الدنيا على خير لأنك تفعل فيها ما تريد

RAZI:93:4/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:4/r5.speaker: author
RAZI:93:4/r5.claim: The Prophet will be reunited with his community in Paradise; the community is like his children, and the Qurʾān calls wives their mothers and asks for spouses and offspring as comfort to the eyes.
RAZI:93:4/r5.anchor: يجتمع عندك أمتك إذ الأمة له كالأولاد

RAZI:93:4/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:4/r6.speaker: author
RAZI:93:4/r6.claim: The Hereafter is better because it is the Prophet's earned possession, whereas this world is not his; even a lesser owned good would be preferable to what is not owned.

RAZI:93:4/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:4/r7.speaker: author
RAZI:93:4/r7.claim: In this world disbelievers attack the Prophet, whereas in the Hereafter his community witnesses for nations, he witnesses for prophets, and God witnesses for him.
RAZI:93:4/r7.anchor: الآخرة خير لك من الأولى لأن في الدنيا الكفار يطعنون فيك أما في الآخرة فأجعل أمتك شهداء على الأمم

RAZI:93:4/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:4/r8.speaker: author
RAZI:93:4/r8.claim: Worldly benefits are few, mixed, and temporary, while the Hereafter's pleasures are abundant, pure, and lasting.
RAZI:93:4/r8.anchor: أن خيرات الدنيا قليلة مشوبة منقطعة

RAZI:93:4/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:4/r9.speaker: author
RAZI:93:4/r9.claim: The wording addresses the Prophet alone because some of his companions would fare badly in the Hereafter; universalizing the promise would be false, while naming only the obedient would expose sinners and hypocrites.

RAZI:93:4/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:4/r10.speaker: author
RAZI:93:4/r10.claim: Rāzī contrasts Moses's assurance that God is with him with Muhammad's assurance that God is with “us,” since Muhammad's companions there were only the Prophet and Abū Bakr, both destined for happiness.
RAZI:93:4/r10.anchor: وأما محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم فالذي كان معه لما كان من أهل السعادة

RAZI:93:4/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:4/r11.speaker: author
RAZI:93:4/r11.claim: A report about Moses says a drought prayer with thousands failed for three days because a talebearer was among them; after God said the talebearer had died, Moses found seventy funeral biers at the prayer place.
RAZI:93:4/r11.anchor: وروي أن موسى عليه السلام خرج للاستسقاء

RAZI:93:4/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:4/r12.speaker: author
RAZI:93:4/r12.claim: The story illustrates God's concealment even of enemies; the saying “if not for elders bowing” hints that this community is favored, since one sinner once held back thousands, while one obedient person brings mercy to sinners.
RAZI:93:4/r12.anchor: فهذا ستره على أعدائه فكيف على أوليائه

TAB-FULL:v1p87/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p87/r1.speaker: الشعبي
TAB-FULL:v1p87/r1.claim: Al-Sha'bi harshly rebuked al-Suddi for interpreting, saying that being beaten with a drum would be better than attending his session.
TAB-FULL:v1p87/r1.anchor: مر الشعبي على السدي وهو يفسر، فقال: «لأن يضرب على استك بالطبل

TAB-FULL:v1p87/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p87/r2.speaker: إبراهيم
TAB-FULL:v1p87/r2.claim: Ibrahim al-Nakha'i remarks that al-Suddi interprets according to the interpretations of the people.
TAB-FULL:v1p87/r2.anchor: عن مسلم بن عبد الرحمن النخعي، قال: كنت مع إبراهيم، فرأى السدي، فقال: «أما إنه يفسر تفسير القوم»

TAB-FULL:v1p87/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p87/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v1p87/r3.claim: Qatada says he knows no one who can keep pace with al-Kalbi in Quran interpretation.
TAB-FULL:v1p87/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، قال: «ما أرى أحدا يجري مع الكلبي في التفسير في عنان»

TAB-FULL:v1p87/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p87/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p87/r4.claim: Tabari divides interpretation into what God alone knows (such as the Hour and other future events), what God taught His Messenger for people through revelation, and Arabic meanings accessible to speakers of the Quran's language.
TAB-FULL:v1p87/r4.anchor: وأن تأويل جميع القرآن على أوجه ثلاثة: أحدها: لا سبيل إلى الوصول إليه، وهو الذي استأثر الله بعلمه

TAB-FULL:v1p87/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p87/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p87/r5.claim: For meanings entrusted to the Prophet, the soundest interpretation relies on established Prophetic reports, whether widely transmitted, carried by reliable narrators, or supported by clear evidence.

TAB-FULL:v1p87/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p87/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p87/r6.claim: For interpretations reached through Arabic, Tabari calls for the clearest proof from circulating Arabic poetry or ordinary speech.
TAB-FULL:v1p87/r6.anchor: وأوضحهم برهانا فيما ترجم وبين من ذلك، مما كان مدركا علمه من جهة اللسان، إما بالشواهد من أشعارهم السائرة
